nodes.label: Amazon SDE-I Tailored CV
nodes.rationale: Led with concurrency, algorithms, and databases instead of recommendation/sequence models to match the Amazon SDE posting's keywords; dropped the math-tutor work entry to make room for a fourth project on one page; header retitled 'Software Engineer | Data Science M.Sc. Student'; forecasting research reworded as 'modular framework across a distributed compute cluster' to surface the posting's scalable/distributed-computing language.

nodes.label: Amazon SDE-I Tailoring Notes
nodes.rationale: Notes logged next to the output because this project stores postings in jobs.json, not the deprecated positions/<id>/ folder referenced by the skill template; includes a self-audit that every concrete CV claim maps to an experience-bank entry.

nodes.label: LoRA Fine-Tuning
nodes.rationale: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method used to adapt Qwen2.5-0.5B to a literary corpus; headline metric for the AI/LLM engineer positioning (perplexity 18.05 to 16.54, QA F1 0.011 to 0.291).

nodes.label: Base CV Visual Template (base_cv.html)
nodes.rationale: Separates visual template (fonts, layout, colors, section order) from the content pool so tailored CVs reuse consistent styling with swapped-in content.

nodes.label: Experience Bank (CV content pool)
nodes.rationale: Acts as the single source of truth for CV tailoring so the tailoring step can verify claims against real experience; inventing content in the bank would defeat the safety design. Deliberately holds more content than fits one page - the tailoring step decides what makes the cut per job. Skills must carry evidence (never a bare list) and each achievement lives in exactly one file to avoid duplication.

nodes.label: CV Tailoring Process
nodes.rationale: Reads a job's requirements, picks the most relevant bank entries, and produces new HTML from the base template. Scans YAML frontmatter at runtime so no manifest file needs maintaining; priority field (1-3) and lowercase hyphen-separated tags drive selection.

nodes.label: LinkedIn Guest API read via navigate+get_page_text. Rationale: the old inject-JS method suffered ~1KB output truncation and content blocks that were properties of javascript_tool's return channel; navigating to the guest endpoints and reading rendered text avoids all of it, though the same rate limits (HTTP 429 ~60 requests) still apply.

nodes.label: SQL Data Applications (Big Data course)
nodes.rationale: Data loaded in 50k-row chunks to keep memory flat; a covering index was verified with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and a timed benchmark showing a 50-80x speedup (150-200 ms down to 2-5 ms); the free-text SQL panel is SELECT-only validated for safety.

nodes.label: Autoencoder Reconstruction-Error Anomaly Detection
nodes.rationale: Anomalies are flagged when reconstruction error of an autoencoder exceeds a threshold; the alignment and thresholding pipeline was built to be reusable across sensor configurations.

nodes.label: Interrupted Time Series Design
nodes.rationale: Chosen because the study looks for a jump at a known event date (public launch of generative-AI writing tools); paired with length-robust lexical-diversity metrics (MTLD, MATTR, HD-D) and sensitivity checks for confounds.

nodes.label: LoRA Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
nodes.rationale: Trains small adapter matrices instead of all model weights, making it feasible to adapt Qwen2.5-0.5B on university GPU resources; two-stage design (continued pre-training then supervised fine-tuning) cut perplexity 18.05 to 16.54 and lifted QA F1 from 0.011 to 0.291.

nodes.label: Conformal Prediction (incl. adaptive conformal inference)
nodes.rationale: Used because it yields calibrated quantile forecasts from any model, letting the scheduling pipeline stay model-agnostic.

nodes.label: Earthquake-Prediction Model Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Started with minimal transformation to see which models naturally fit the data (Naive Bayes won); LSTM was tried for the sequential structure but underperformed and was documented as an honest negative result.

nodes.label: LLM Fine-Tuning with LoRA (Sherlock Holmes corpus)
nodes.norm_label: llm fine-tuning with lora (sherlock holmes corpus)

nodes.label: Multithreaded Client-Server Trivia Game
nodes.rationale: UDP broadcast chosen for game discovery, TCP for reliable play; one thread per player with locks, events, and barriers to keep shared game state consistent under disconnects, timeouts, and race conditions.

nodes.label: Large-Scale Network & Graph Analysis
nodes.rationale: The 6.85 GB / 429M-edge chess graph could not fit in memory, so it was stream-aggregated with polars into a compact weighted edge list (out-of-core processing) instead of being loaded whole.

nodes.label: S7comm Industrial-Protocol Packet Parser
nodes.rationale: Drives tshark (Wireshark's CLI engine) rather than reimplementing capture parsing; matches request/response PDUs by reference and computes byte/bit offsets in DB memory blocks to turn raw industrial traffic into labeled sensor time series.

nodes.label: Wikipedia Search Engine (Information Retrieval)
nodes.rationale: Per-posting BM25 contributions were precomputed to minimize query-time work; the title-only index answered in about 0.6 s while adding the body index reached higher quality at about 6.5 s, and the configuration was chosen to balance latency and relevance.

nodes.label: Time-Series Forecasting Benchmark (Master's Research)
nodes.rationale: Benchmarks 30+ models on Profinet interarrival times, then uses quantile forecasts in an evaluate-rank(CRPS)-simulate pipeline so a discrete-event simulator can slot low-priority packets between high-priority ones, approaching time-sensitive-networking safety on commodity hardware.

nodes.label: Tweet Device Classification (Android vs iPhone NLP)
nodes.norm_label: tweet device classification (android vs iphone nlp)
nodes.rationale: Five model families compared under 5-fold stratified cross-validation with grid search; fine-tuned DistilBERT won (F1 0.862) while stylometric and temporal features drove the classical models.

nodes.label: LLM-Agent User-Behavior Simulation (MovieLens)
nodes.rationale: LLM agents seeded with real MovieLens-32M preferences simulate three behavioral types (herder, truthful, strategic) to generate labeled training data for a downstream user-type classifier; five-phase config-driven pipeline with SLURM for heavy phases.

nodes.label: Machine Learning Skills Cluster
nodes.rationale: Every skill is backed by an explicit pointer to the research project where it was used (evidence-based skills, never a bare list); on the CV, skill families matching the job posting are promoted to the front of the comma-separated line.

nodes.label: Field Ownership - one writer per field, field-scoped read-modify-write. Rationale: multiple independent writers (scraper, Gmail task, dashboard, CV skill) share one jobs.json without a server or database; giving each field exactly one owner and patching only owned fields prevents writers from clobbering each other.
nodes.norm_label: field ownership - one writer per field, field-scoped read-modify-write. rationale: multiple independent writers (scraper, gmail task, dashboard, cv skill) share one jobs.json without a server or database; giving each field exactly one owner and patching only owned fields prevents writers from clobbering each other.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Status Moves. Rationale: Gmail may only rank statuses applied < rejected < interview < offer and move up, only when the email is newer than status_changed_at, so an automated classifier can never downgrade a state the user set and a user click always wins.

nodes.label: Title Pre-filter before detail fetch. Rationale: applying gates 2a-2d' to card titles before opening detail pages halves the detail fetches; never pre-filter on years because years need the detail text.

nodes.label: Folder Link via File System Access API. Rationale: the dashboard is a single static HTML file with no server; linking the project folder once lets every click be persisted straight into jobs.json with field-scoped patches, while localStorage keeps edits usable when no folder is linked.
